entry_points.text: Under ●3, a defendant who ●2 is served with the summons and complaint on ●1. What is the last day to serve an answer?

params.description: the calendar date on which the summons and complaint were served on the defendant, including weekday if given
params.validity_range: Must be a valid calendar date (real day, month, and year) that is a day on which service occurred; the triggering date must be a real date so that day counting is defined. Weekday label, if present, must match the actual weekday of that date. Dates far in the past or future are logically valid but may fall under different holiday calendars or rule versions.

params.description: the waiver status of service for the defendant, stating whether the defendant waived formal service or not
params.validity_range: Must be a binary status: either the defendant did not waive service (so the standard 21-day answer period under Rule 12(a)(1)(A)(i) applies) or the defendant waived service (a different period applies, such as 60 days after the waiver request was sent under Rule 4(d)). Any other phrasing must reduce to one of these two states.

params.description: the governing procedural rule that sets the time to serve an answer, cited by rule number
params.validity_range: Must identify a rule that prescribes a response deadline measured from service of a pleading or summons. Rule 12(a) covers answers to complaints in federal court; other rules or jurisdictions (for example state procedure or responses to counterclaims) prescribe different periods, so the parameter selects which period-length rule applies.

entry_points.text: Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 12(a), a defendant who did not waive service is served with the summons and complaint on Friday, March 6, 2026. What is the last day to serve an answer?
